title: Reliability Integration Lab — Pilot Operator Playbook
body:
Purpose:
This playbook captures the operator-facing runbook and tactical decisions for the Reliability Integration Lab pilot. The goal of the Lab is to validate cross-functional processes for defining, measuring, and operating SLOs for a set of canonical model-serving services before wider org rollout.

Audience:
- SREs running the pilot oncall shifts
- Product and infra engineers taking part in the integration experiments
- Observability and tooling owners who will ship dashboards/alerts
- Solutions/SEs coordinating customer-impact scenarios

High-level pilot goals (what success looks like):
- End-to-end SLO lifecycle validated for 3 services: inference-api, routing-proxy, kv-cache
- Measurement pipeline end-to-end (metric -> alert -> incident -> postmortem) operational with owned dashboards and automated error-budget meter
- Two 2-week canaries demonstrating rollback/fallback policies and automated routing under degraded capacity
- Training: 10 engineers can run through the incident playbook within 45 minutes and re-establish green status within target RTO

Scope (in/out):
- In: request latency SLOs (p95/p99), availability SLOs, CPU/GPU resource throttling experiments, prefix cache eviction effects, synthetic workload injection
- Out: billing model changes, model quality drift detection (will be covered separately by Optimize team)

SLO candidates and rationale (pilot baseline):
- inference-api: availability 99.9% (30d rolling), request p95 < 180ms (traffic-weighted) — product-facing, customer latency matters
- routing-proxy: availability 99.95% (30d), p99 < 250ms — critical path for multi-region routing
- kv-cache: cache hit-rate >= 80% for tail-heavy prompt sets; availability 99.5% — impacts token cost and downstream latency

Measurement windows and burn rate policies:
- Window = 30d rolling for availability; 7d rolling for latency SLOs used in short-term experiments
- Error budget policy: automated throttle — when cumulative burn rate > 50% in 7d, trigger traffic shaping to Dedicated capacity and notify product owners
- Escalation: burn > 80% in 24h triggers leadership pager and rollback to previous stable model/container image

Experiment phases and timeline (pilot quarter):
- Phase 0 (discovery) — 2026-09-15 to 2026-09-26: map dependencies, confirm telemetry; owners assigned
- Phase 1 (integration lab) — 2026-09-27 to 2026-10-10: synthetic workload runs, dashboard shipping, basic alerts configured
- Phase 2 (canary + oncall drills) — 2026-10-11 to 2026-10-24: two canary windows with deliberate capacity throttles and failovers
- Phase 3 (retro + handoff) — 2026-10-25 to 2026-10-31: collect learnings, adjust runbooks, prepare rollout backlog

Operator runbook (quick reference):
- Green -> Yellow -> Red states defined in observable panel
- Oncall steps for Yellow:
  1) Check error-budget panel and alert history
  2) Verify recent deploys (git SHA, model revision)
  3) If latency regressions only and error budget burn < 30% -> change batching config (reduce batch_size by 10%) and monitor for 15m
  4) If hit-rate drop on kv-cache -> trigger cache-warm job for hot prefixes, escalate to infra if eviction rate > 5%/min
- Oncall steps for Red (sustained burn or availability drop):
  1) Open incident in the template (use channel #ril-incidents)
  2) Run automated rollback to previous model/container variant OR trigger fallback routing to a lower-cost variant (policy in routing-proxy)
  3) Notify product owner, SRE lead, and infra lead, include current error budget percentage and affected routes
  4) Execute mitigation playbook to restore traffic to Dedicated capacity if available

Dashboards and alerts to ship before Phase 1 completion:
- Error budget overview (per-service, 7d/30d lenses)
- Latency histograms (p50/p95/p99) + traffic volume with annotations for deploys
- Cache telemetry (hit-rate, eviction-rate, size-variance)
- Resource saturation panels (GPU util, VRAM pressure, per-host thread-pools)
- Synthetic traffic scoreboard showing injected workload and observed latency
- Alerts: latency p99 > threshold sustained for 3m; availability drop > 0.5% in 5m; cache hit-rate drop > 10% in 10m

Rollout and rollback policy (short):
- Canary rollout window: 10% traffic -> 30% -> 100% with 30min observation gates; automatic rollback on critical alert or burn > 40% in 1h
- Fallback: routing-proxy policy supports downgrade to quantized model variant (lower cost, lower accuracy) under availability pressure; decision owned by product oncall

Training and exercises:
- 2-hour workshop for SREs + product engineers covering playbook walkthrough, dashboard reading, and simulated incident (tools: chaos-monkey-lite, traffic-replayer)
- Checklist for trainees: understand SLO math, know where the error budget lives, run a manual cache-warm job, trigger a safe rollback

Handoff checklist for teams at end of pilot:
- Metrics: dashboards live and annotated, alert thresholds validated
- Docs: runbook reviewed and assigned, postmortem template added to Confluence page
- Automation: basic auto-rollback pipeline and traffic-shaping scripts checked into ops repo
- Training: at least 2 engineers from each product team completed the workshop and can run the drill

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Synthetic workload not representative of real customer tails -> Mitigation: run small shadowing experiment with 1% production traffic during Phase 2
- Risk: Observability gaps for per-tenant latency -> Mitigation: add tagging at ingress and ensure sampling preserves tenant id for latency traces
- Risk: Rollback causes transient surge leading to cascading failures -> Mitigation: autoscaling policy add cooldown and circuit-breaker in routing proxy

Open questions (needs decisions):
- Which exact traffic slices count as ‘critical customers’ for targeted canaries? (Product to provide list)
- Error budget handoff: who has final approval to pull fallback routing in a cross-region outage? (SRE lead or Product ops?)
- Should we use 30d or 60d window for availability SLOs for services that are low-traffic?

Action items (owners and target dates):
- Lukas: finalize dashboard templates and push Grafana JSON by 2026-09-22
- Chen: implement synthetic workload scripts + runbook callouts by 2026-09-30
- Priya: coordinate product owner list and critical-customer targets by 2026-09-20
- Daniel: wire auto-rollback pipeline (feature branch) and create demo PR by 2026-10-05
- Aisha (owner): schedule the 2-hour workshop and send calendar invites by 2026-10-02

Post-pilot artifacts to create:
- Annotated incident timeline (example incident from canary 2)
- Editable runbook (single-file) with step-by-step automation commands
- Handoff report and rollout recommendations for the reliability council

Notes to self (work-in-progress style, keep):
- Expect a lot of noise when simulating GPU pressure — need to tune the synthetic driver to avoid saturating cluster control plane metrics
- Keep the Lexicon short: use ‘error budget’ not ‘eb’ in public pages to reduce confusion
- Capture any small config changes as PRs with well-formed rollbacks so we can rehearse the full path

References & quick links:
- Confluence: Integration Lab Home (linked_artifacts above)
- Jira backlog: JIRA-3142, JIRA-3199 (observability gaps), JIRA-3221 (rollback pipeline)
- Ops repo: github.com/redwood-inference/ops-playbooks (see pilot branch)

Revision history:
- 2026-09-15: initial draft created by Aisha
- 2026-09-20: added pilot timeline and owner assignments (Priya input)
- 2026-10-03: updated runbook steps and canary gating criteria after sync with Lukas

End of playbook.
